forces.title: Emerging growth sectors increase raw materials demand
forces.description: New growth sectors like semiconductors, data centers, green hydrogen, and advanced manufacturing are expected to significantly increase demand for various raw materials. This expansion across high-tech and industrial segments will drive consumption of specialty chemicals, industrial gases, and metals, creating substantial opportunities for the Materials sector. The long-term trajectory for these sectors ensures sustained demand for key material inputs, bolstering growth and investment in the Indian materials industry.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Waste conversion into industrial feedstock drives value creation
forces.description: India is transforming material flows from waste into income, employment, and industrial feedstock. This structural shift redefines waste management from a disposal burden to an economic input, fostering value creation in secondary materials markets. For the Materials sector, this means new sources of raw materials from waste-to-energy, biomethanation, and critical mineral recovery, driving investment opportunities and job creation across the supply chain, bolstering circular economy principles and long-term sustainability.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Climate change intensifies water stress, impacting production
forces.description: India's average temperature is projected to rise by 1.2–1.8°C by 2050, intensifying evaporation and drought risk, directly threatening water availability. This climate-induced water stress poses a significant key risk to water-intensive industries within the Materials sector, such as chemicals, metals, and paper. Water scarcity can lead to increased operational costs, production curtailments, and challenges in maintaining output, compelling companies to invest in water conservation and alternative sourcing strategies for long-term resilience.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Industrial water demand triples, boosting water treatment
forces.description: Demand for water from manufacturing is projected to more than triple from 16 BCM to 50 BCM by 2030, driven by rapid scaling in water-intensive sectors like semiconductors, data centres, and green hydrogen production. This surge in industrial water demand creates a significant tailwind for companies providing water treatment chemicals (IN020101) and construction materials (IN020201, IN020202) for new and advanced water treatment infrastructure, ensuring water security for industrial growth and promoting sector-wide investment.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Water quality degradation increases treatment demand and costs
forces.description: Rapid urbanization, industrial growth, untreated sewage discharge, and agricultural runoff significantly reduce the volume of usable freshwater. This water quality degradation poses a key risk, as it exacerbates water stress and necessitates increased investment in advanced water treatment solutions. Consequently, this trend will drive higher demand for specialty chemicals (IN020101) used in water treatment and construction materials (IN020201, IN020202) for new treatment infrastructure, increasing operational costs for industries and requiring more complex solutions.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: New SWM Rules enforce circular economy, boost demand
forces.description: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, integrate circular economy and Extended Producer Responsibility principles into municipal waste governance. This structural change drives demand for secondary materials, recycling infrastructure, and waste processing technologies. The mandate for four-stream segregation and increased RDF usage directly benefits IN0207 Containers & Packaging, IN0203 Metals & Mining, and IN0205 Paper & Forest Products by improving feedstock quality and expanding markets for recovered resources, promoting a more sustainable materials ecosystem.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Stricter SWM regulations boost waste processing demand
forces.description: New Solid Waste Management Rules (2026) mandate environmental compensation for non-compliance and tighten landfill restrictions, allowing only inert waste. The Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) mandate requires cement and waste-to-energy plants to raise RDF usage from 5% to 15% over six years. This structural change significantly boosts demand for waste processing equipment, biomethanation, and materials recovery, directly benefiting IN020201 Cement & Concrete Products as RDF off-takers and promoting broader materials recovery, while acting as a headwind for non-compliant entities.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: RDF mandate de-risks waste processing investment
forces.description: The Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) ramp-up mandate in the 2026 SWM Rules guarantees off-take for cement co-processing over the next six years. This tailwind de-risks investment in Material Recovery Facilities (MRF) and mechanical-biological treatment capacity by providing assured demand for RDF. It incentivizes ULBs to deliver segregated, contamination-controlled dry waste, directly benefiting the waste-to-energy sector and supporting the circular economy for materials by providing reliable feedstock streams.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Sustainability focus drives green chemicals market growth
forces.description: In the specialty chemicals sector (IN020101), manufacturers are increasingly focusing on green solvents, biodegradable surfactants, and bio-based polymers. This structural change is driving significant growth in India’s green chemicals market, which is expected to grow at a CAGR of over 10% and exceed US$ 15 billion by 2027. This shift promotes sustainable manufacturing practices and creates substantial opportunities for innovation and investment in environmentally friendly chemical solutions for the medium to long term.
forces.source_title: Chemicals Industry In India

forces.title: PLI scheme boosts ACC battery and critical minerals demand
forces.description: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage, which has awarded 40 GWh of manufacturing capacity, and a separate rare earth magnet scheme, acts as a strong tailwind. These initiatives drive demand for critical minerals like lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements (IN020304), as well as related specialty chemicals (IN020101). This policy support fosters domestic production and reduces import dependence, creating significant long-term growth opportunities for the Materials sector.
forces.source_title: Chips, phones, and the Viksit Bharat playbook

forces.title: Mineral production growth driven by downstream industries
forces.description: Increased production of iron ore (up to 300 MT), limestone (up to 450 MT), and coal (up to 1 billion tonnes) is underpinned by rising downstream consumption in sectors like steel, cement, and power. This tailwind ensures sustained demand for these primary materials (IN020301, IN020304, IN020201) from key industrial users, driving continued growth in the mining and basic materials sub-industries over the long term. This solidifies their market position and supports investment in extraction and processing capabilities.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: National Critical Mineral Mission boosts resource security
forces.description: The INR 34,300 crore National Critical Mineral Mission, backed by rare-earth corridors and MMDR liberalization, with 30+ blocks auctioned and 100+ expected, is a strong tailwind. This initiative drives exploration, extraction, and processing of critical minerals (IN020304) like lithium, cobalt, and rare earths, enhancing India's resource security. The significant government investment and policy support create long-term growth opportunities, reducing import dependence and establishing a robust domestic supply chain for key industrial inputs.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: Foreign dominance in critical mineral processing creates vulnerability
forces.description: China's dominant position in critical-mineral processing equipment presents a strategic vulnerability for India, as access can be constrained by geopolitical factors. This key risk highlights India's dependence on foreign technology and machinery for refining critical minerals (IN020304). Building a domestic base for this equipment is not only an industrial opportunity but a matter of resource security, necessitating long-term strategic investment to reduce reliance and ensure resilient supply chains for essential industrial inputs.
forces.source_title: Pressing the Throttle: Unlocking India’s Mining and Construction Equipment Industry’s Potential

forces.title: LNG supply disruptions threaten fertilizer costs and food security
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions causing LNG flow disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz pose a key risk for India's IN020104 Fertilisers sector. Such disruptions rapidly cascade into fertilizer supply risks, price volatility, and fiscal pressure, as LNG is a critical hydrocarbon feedstock for ammonia production. This directly impacts fertilizer output and costs, threatening agricultural productivity and food security. The near to medium-term volatility underscores India's vulnerability to concentrated global energy routes, necessitating diversification and resilience strategies.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Biogas offers sustainable organic fertilizer alternative
forces.description: The processing of biogas byproduct (digestate) into organic fertilizers like phosphate-rich organic manure (PROM) offers a significant upside driver for IN020104 Fertilisers. This circular approach reduces dependence on synthetic fertilizers while improving soil quality and lowering input costs for farmers. By integrating waste, energy, and agriculture, it creates a dual advantage, supporting both environmental sustainability and agricultural resilience. This long-term opportunity enhances the value chain for organic materials and reduces reliance on imported chemical inputs.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Nano Urea adoption reduces import dependency for fertilizers
forces.description: India's shift towards Nano Urea as an alternative to conventional urea represents a structural change for IN020104 Fertilisers. This technological advancement aims to reduce dependence on imported LNG and urea, increasing self-reliance in a critical agricultural input. The long-term impact involves transforming the fertilizer industry by lowering import costs and enhancing domestic production capabilities, thereby strengthening national food security and reducing exposure to global supply chain volatility.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Robust industrial activity boosts steel and cement demand
forces.description: The rebound in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), led by manufacturing and mining, indicates robust industrial activity. This creates a tailwind for the Materials sector, specifically for IN020301 Steel & Ferrous Metals and IN020201 Cement & Concrete Products, as steel consumption and cement production have increased. This positive trend, driven by broader economic activity, signals improved demand for key building materials and industrial inputs, enhancing their market performance in the near term.
forces.source_title: Indian Banking Sector: Top Updates: Banking Sector RoundUp - Q1FY26

forces.title: Government capital expenditure drives cement demand
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026-27's record allocation of Rs. 12.2 lakh crore towards capital expenditure for infrastructure development serves as a significant tailwind. This directly creates demand opportunities for IN020201 Cement & Concrete Products across roads, railways, logistics, urban infrastructure, and industrial corridors. Major railway projects with planned investments of Rs. 1.53 lakh crore further contribute to this incremental demand, ensuring sustained growth and investment in the cement sector over the medium term.
forces.source_title: Cement Industry In India

forces.title: Private sector investment boosts cement production capacity
forces.description: India's top cement producers are set to invest approximately Rs. 1,20,000 crore in capital expenditure between FY26 and FY28, representing a 50% increase over the previous three years. This substantial private sector investment acts as a strong tailwind, indicating high industry confidence and robust expansion plans. It will significantly boost production capacity for IN020201 Cement & Concrete Products, catering to growing infrastructure and housing demands, ensuring medium-term growth and market stability.
forces.source_title: Cement Industry In India

forces.title: Policy support enhances metals and mining competitiveness
forces.description: The FY27 Budget strengthens India’s metals and mining sector (IG0203) through measures like mineral corridors and duty exemptions for critical minerals. This policy tailwind, combined with strong engineering capabilities and a robust manufacturing base, enhances domestic production and reduces import dependence. It improves India’s global competitiveness in value-added metal exports, creating long-term growth prospects across the sector, particularly for diversified mining and critical minerals (IN020304).
forces.source_title: Metals And Mining Industry In India

forces.title: Rising non-ferrous metal prices boost industry revenue
forces.description: Non-ferrous metals like copper, aluminium, and zinc recorded significant price increases in the September 2025 quarter (3.1%, 6.9%, and 7.2% respectively). This tailwind is driven by strong industrial demand, increased infrastructure activity, and limited global supply, leading to a rally in major Indian metal stocks. The price appreciation directly boosts revenue and profitability for IN020303 Copper and IN020302 Aluminium & Non-Ferrous Metals sub-industries in the near term, improving their financial performance and market sentiment.
forces.source_title: Metals And Mining Industry In India

forces.title: Reduced GST on paper packaging drives demand
forces.description: The reduction of GST on packing paper, cartons, and corrugated boxes to 5% serves as a significant tailwind for IN020701 Paper & Cardboard Packaging. This policy change lowers packaging and logistics costs for e-commerce shipments, supporting growth in the e-commerce and food processing sectors. By making packaging more cost-efficient, it stimulates increased demand for paper and cardboard products, fostering market expansion and improving profitability for manufacturers in the medium term.
forces.source_title: Paper And Packaging Industry In India

forces.title: Government pushes for sustainable packaging materials
forces.description: The government's plan to adopt initiatives focused on sustainable manufacturing, minimizing plastic packaging, and using sustainable materials represents a structural change for the IG0207 Containers & Packaging sector. This policy push will drive demand for eco-friendly packaging solutions, promoting innovation and shifting industry practices towards greener alternatives. It creates long-term opportunities for manufacturers to develop and implement sustainable materials and production methods, aligning the sector with environmental goals and consumer preferences.
forces.source_title: Paper And Packaging Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Circular economy crucial for India's long-term resource security and competitiveness
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that the transition to a circular economy is not merely an environmental goal but an economic imperative for India. By treating water, wastewater, solid waste, and recovered materials as interconnected elements, India can ensure long-term resource security, enhance industrial competitiveness, and foster urban resilience. This shift from an infrastructure-led to an outcomes-led, digitally enabled model will unlock significant economic opportunities through resource recovery and reuse, securing sustainable growth for the Materials sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

viewpoints.title: Solid waste management offers compelling economic opportunities for private investment
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts that solid waste management should be recognized as a compelling economic opportunity, moving beyond its traditional role as a municipal cost center. With regional aggregation, predictable tipping-fee mechanisms, and dependable demand for recovered energy and recyclable materials, the sector can attract substantial private investment. This strategic shift transforms discarded materials into valuable economic inputs, fostering income, employment, and industrial feedstock streams, which is a positive outlook for materials recovery and processing sub-industries.
viewpoints.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

viewpoints.title: Elevated SWM Rules signal greater enforcement, investment in waste processing
viewpoints.description: KPMG views the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and the Supreme Court's oversight as transforming municipal waste governance into a constitutional imperative. This heightened scrutiny and judicial intervention will drive stricter compliance and increased investment in waste processing and resource recovery. The endorsement of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) model for SWM further attracts private capital and specialized expertise, fostering growth for industries involved in waste-to-value solutions within the Materials sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

viewpoints.title: Indian writing & printing paper industry faces sustained margin pressure
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings indicates a cautious-negative outlook for India’s writing and printing paper industry. Realizations are under pressure due to a sharp rise in low-priced imports, particularly from China and ASEAN, which grew over 80% from FY21-FY26. Elevated raw material costs, combined with GST distortions and higher freight/war-risk insurance, are squeezing margins. The potential redirection of surplus global supply to India further intensifies import competition, making a meaningful recovery in profitability unlikely in the near term for IN020501.

viewpoints.title: UK FTA enhances competitiveness for Indian tyre and rubber manufacturers
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports a positive outlook for Indian tyre and rubber manufacturers due to the India-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement. The immediate elimination of import duties on tyre and rubber products exported to the UK is expected to provide Indian companies with a significant price advantage. This will deepen their presence in the British market and build on existing export momentum, benefiting sub-industries like IN020102 (synthetic rubber) and IN020101 (carbon black, a key input for tyres).

viewpoints.title: Government signals strong growth for India's steel sector by 2047
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights the government's positive outlook for India's steel sector, targeting 500 MT production capacity by 2047. This ambition is supported by robust domestic demand, expanding exports, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, green steel initiatives, and greater global market access. These policy commitments and demand drivers are expected to fuel substantial capacity expansion and overall growth for the IN020301 Steel & Ferrous Metals sub-industry.

viewpoints.title: Indian specialty chemicals market poised for sustained growth by 2033
viewpoints.description: IBEF's analysis presents a positive outlook for the Indian specialty chemicals market, valued at US$ 64.5 billion in 2024 and projected to reach US$ 92.6 billion by 2033 at a CAGR of 3.80%. This growth is driven by rising demand from key end-user sectors like agriculture, construction, automotive, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. Increasing industrialization, urbanization, product innovation, and supportive government policies further bolster the sector's expansion, enhancing profitability and investment in IN020101.

viewpoints.title: India's fertiliser system vulnerable to external energy shocks
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights a cautious-negative outlook for India's fertiliser system, citing its structural exposure to external energy shocks. The heavy dependence on imported LNG for ammonia production, concentrated sourcing from the Gulf, and chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz create systemic fragility. Geopolitical disruptions lead to supply risks, price volatility, and fiscal pressure for IN020104 Fertilisers. Current stabilisation measures only cushion impact, leaving the underlying dependency unaddressed, posing a continuous risk to cost and supply.
viewpoints.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

viewpoints.title: Cement sector poised for robust growth, driven by infrastructure and housing
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports a positive outlook for India’s cement sector, with ICRA projecting 7–8% volume growth in FY27 due to sustained demand from housing and infrastructure. CRISIL Ratings indicates planned capacity additions of 150-160 MT between FY25-FY28. Operating profits are expected to rise by 12-18% in FY26. These trends reflect robust demand, favorable realizations, and stable input costs, ensuring continued expansion and profitability for IN020201 Cement & Concrete Products.
